summary: Materialized and read ARIST-MET-II-1, Metaphysics II.1 993b24–31 and context, and AQUINAS-ST-I-Q13-A5 co. and ad 1 and AQUINAS-ST-I-Q2-A3 quarta via. Aristotle specifies the synonymous quality, gives fire/heat and then truth; the old claim binding incorrectly classified an unrestricted premise as sourced. Rebound the claim to a distinct pairwise restricted interpretation requiring a shared account under which both entities possess the quality. This is an explicit conservative interpretation of the Greek, not a proof that every causal use satisfies it. Aquinas distinguishes human generation as univocal from the sun as non-univocal agent, and divine names as analogical rather than purely equivocal; neither analogy nor the attribution order is identified with synonymy. The quarta via invokes a converse maximum-to-cause principle; the example does not justify that universal converse. A three-entity interpretation has one same-account edge with comparison and a changed-account edge without it; it witnesses formal non-implication, not metaphysical possibility. Unrestricted implies restricted, with no converse on this interpretation. No root theorem type or premise changes and no closure follows.
